newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on indicators, Latam markets.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on indicators, Latam markets.

text.p: Argentine bonds put in a strong performance Monday, helped by general flows into the Latin American region although activity was still fairly slim.
"The market rose with the whole region," said a trader at a large foreign bank. The market began to rise last week after several U.S. indicators showed moderating U.S. growth.
With market friendly Argentine indicators released late Friday and this session, bonds were given an additional boost.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 3/4 to 83-6/8, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.55 to 119.90.
The Economy Ministry said Monday consumer prices rose 0.5 percent in October from the previous month, compared with 0.3 percent in October 1995 and 0.2 percent in September this year.
Wholesale prices were up 0.5 percent, compared with 0.2 percent in October last year and 1.2 percent a month earlier.
Another trader said the market "looks attractive at these levels."
Before the gains in the market at the end of last week, Argentine bonds slumped for about 10 days as many investors booked profits after the large gains clocked up this year.
But the second trader reckoned that some investors may now be returning to the market, particularly those that still have funds in cash to invest before the end of the year.
The Economy Ministry said Friday tax revenue in October was $3.72 billion, 12.5 percent higher than the same month a year earlier and 12.9 percent up on September.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.85 percent from 6.95 percent.
